design.row_status: 0=NOT_AVAILABLE (no compo row), 1=PARTIAL (some required field missing), 2=CHECKED (all required fields present and in physical range, both C3 and C4 applicable), 3=FAIL (present but out of physical range)
design.presence_flags: yn_present, yp_present, ye_present, ymu_present, abar_present, zbar_present, yh_present - per-row logical; a written zero is True, a missing entry is False (the zero-vs-missing distinction)
design.c3_applicable: per-row logical; True iff the complete baryon inventory needed for Yn+Yp+Yh=1 is present (Yn, Yp, Yh all present)
design.c4_applicable: per-row logical; True iff the complete charge inventory needed for Yp+(Z/A)Yh=Ye+Ymu is present (Yp, Abar>0, Zbar, Yh, Ye, Ymu all present)
design.independent_per_row: C3 and C4 are assessed independently per row; a row may be C3-applicable without C4 (e.g. missing Ymu) or vice versa (e.g. missing Yn)
design.global_composition_available_preserved: the legacy global composition_available boolean is preserved for backward compatibility (set True iff any nonzero fraction is read); it is NOT used as the per-row authority

implementation.fortran_types: fortran_eos/src/compose_eos_types.f90 - added 10 allocatable arrays to eos_data_t (row_status, *_present, c3_applicable, c4_applicable); allocate_eos initializes them to NOT_AVAILABLE/False
implementation.fortran_parser: fortran_eos/src/compose_eos_io.f90 read_compose - per-row presence flags set as each field is read; per-row range check sets FAIL only on offending rows (the read succeeds so partial-coverage sources do not abort the whole read); C3/C4 applicability computed per row after all rows are read
implementation.fortran_csv_round_trip: write_internal_csv writes 10 new columns (row_status + 7 presence + 2 applicability); read_internal_csv accepts both the legacy 17-column and the new 27-column CSV (legacy -> defaults)
implementation.python_eos_data: python_frontend/compose_eos/eos_data.py - EOSData dataclass gained 10 mask fields; from_internal_directory reads them with backward-compat defaults; write_internal_directory derives safe defaults if a caller constructed EOSData directly (reconstruct_master path); copy() round-trips them; bool columns converted via int to avoid bool('0') being True
